scope: Independent adversarial review of all 14 R7 production changes against deployed R6. Production and tests were read only; this reviewer authored only this report.
verified_checks: Concrete pending-list race repaired: Before captures a monotonic generation watermark under the pending lock; each native submission carries its own local ticket; After retires matching identities only through that generation. A later Reset/re-recorded generation cannot be mistaken for the older submitted recording.

Generation retirement remains conservative for late tags, empty tickets, multiple lists and overlapping calls. No lock spans native Execute, no per-call heap allocation or shared/TLS ticket was added, and later generations retain their own submission/discard requirement.

Progress callbacks follow actual native Execute and After while submission admission is alive. Polling also acquires submission admission. Fixed entries refer only to already-held queues, with at most eight separately owned diagnostic fences and one unresolved marker per queue.

Progress signals use fresh start timestamps, at least 1000 ms between successful signal starts per queue, and bounded creation attempts. Marker failure or UINT64_MAX stops that probe; neither event changes game/FG state or grants cleanup permission. Driver methods run outside the lifetime registry mutex.

Diagnostic fence release still requires the separate existing full-GPU-drain and closed-admission teardown proof. Soft resets retain probes. Marker completion is never substituted for lifetime/allocator fences or all-GPU-idle evidence.

Tracked Release keeps the existing temporary AddRef/probe/metadata-cleanup/final-Release order and mutex coverage. Added timing shares one 1/64 sampling choice across stages; no speculative lifetime rewrite was introduced.

Allocation descriptors and immediate caller module/RVA are copied from existing creation boundaries without additional GetDesc, QI or allocation-size queries. GPU objects are not retained by diagnostics; generation-checked notifier accounting and installer/uninstaller failure behavior are preserved.

The fixed 4096-slot detail workspace is sorted after the ledger copy lock is released. Bounded top8 live and positive-net-growth groups use matching metadata keys; only complete successful snapshots advance the growth baseline. Failed locks, disappearing/recreated groups and timestamp rewind are handled explicitly.

GpuAllocationTracking is a startup-only diagnostic opt-out, initialized before installation. Disabled observation skips new detours and observation-side driver/COM calls; existing destruction callbacks still retire safely.

Monitor output distinguishes observed LOCAL budget/usage, tracked live allocation estimates, creation age, net growth, cumulative releases, native Present CPU time and sampled queue progress. Every output line consumes the shared 1024-line cap; detail output shows at most two live and two growth groups.
No arbitrary game-resource Release, eviction, flushing, RAM-spill policy, forced resource destruction or new CPU fence wait was introduced.

All 241 tracked shader paths and all seven FG input files match R6 byte-for-byte. Config changes only add the diagnostic startup option; the 1.5 upscale ratio, color/HDR/exposure formulas, selected/maximum multiplier behavior and pacing algorithms are preserved. Exact body/file evidence is in QUALITY_REVIEW.json.

independently_executed_checks.coverage: Exact pinned deployed-R6 negative control requires the late-After/new-generation assertion failure; actual R7 methods test marker cadence, slow creation, pending coalescing, device-removed sentinel, Signal/create failures, held admission, separate teardown proof and context recreation.

Actual Execute hook in both branches forwards once outside registry lock, passes the local generation ticket, and holds admission through After and progress. Actual tracked Release preserves temporary pin, cleanup, final release and shared 1/64 sampling.

Nine subchecks cover actual COM observer/adapter and installer boundaries, balanced temporary references, notifier failure/ABA/pool limits, copied descriptors and unchanged query counts, startup-off, concurrent ledger snapshots, top8 live/growth, baseline intervals, module/RVA classification and transactional detach rollback.
Production state/timing and extracted actual log formatting; pressure hysteresis, observed memory windows, live2/growth2 groups, missing baseline, detail cadence and total 1024-line cap.

Actual lifecycle/Execute/Reset/pending methods including empty ticket, Reset-retag-before-old-After and overlapping selective batches; complete Present/Present1 lifetime plus provider-disable rollback and context resume.

runtime_limitations: No Cyberpunk 2077, Night City-to-Dogtown transition, real Intel XeFG execution, displayed-FPS measurement, image comparison or long-session recovery was performed by this reviewer.

CPU harnesses execute production logic with explicit fake SDK/COM/driver boundaries. They do not establish Windows Detours ABI/runtime behavior, GPU scheduling, real memory pressure, driver latency or device-specific performance; separate Windows CI and game validation are required.

The R6 log shows memory-pressure/native-Present correlation and substantially different LOCAL-budget and tracked-live changes. It does not prove that the generation race caused the reported slowdown or that 2.5 GiB of cumulative releases is instantly reclaimable, unused or leaked VRAM.

Progress covers only the latest tracked XeFG queues. A completed marker proves progress through its position on that queue, not all-queue GPU idleness, all game submission coverage, global resource safety or FPS recovery. Signal-to-first-CPU-poll time is an observation upper bound, not GPU execution duration.

Allocation accounting remains partial: selected creation APIs, allocations at least 1 MiB, hooks installed after startup, notifier support, fixed 4096 capacity and immediate caller attribution. Live estimates and provisional peaks are not resident VRAM; object age does not show unused resources. Growth is net change between successful snapshots, not intervening churn.

Diagnostics have unmeasured real-device overhead. Eligible allocations take a timestamp; copying up to 4096 entries holds the existing ledger lock briefly and can delay Track/Retire. Sorting/logging and bounded driver CreateFence/Signal/GetCompletedValue calls cost CPU time and may themselves stall inside a driver. No lock-free or zero-overhead claim is made.

Fixed CPU workspaces and the notifier callback module deliberately remain alive until process exit, without retaining game GPU references. Startup allocation opt-out permits a controlled overhead comparison after restart.

Polling is rate-limited by cycle start, and snapshot/timing samples can be delayed, skipped or approximately split across counter windows. Existing inherited GPU/UI waits remain; this change does not eliminate every stall or repair arbitrary device removal.

The generation watermark can conservatively retain a recording created after the snapshot until its own later observed submission/reset; avoiding false retirement is intentional. No timeout frees such recordings.

Source checks preserve configured rendering algorithms but cannot establish identical visual output or full gameplay recovery on hardware. Final payload/INI/binary identity is audited separately by the builder.
